title: Where the Figure Went

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: The figure goes up the road in a box and comes back in a loaf, a glance and a space at the row's end. Ask the pot, ask the weather; neither will give you the number.
epigraph.attribution: A saying at the well in Low Kiln, in the kiln month

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-ninety-two-to-one-hundred-and-ninety-four-day-old body carried everywhere and told by nobody — six months and twelve days to six months and fourteen days, no roof with a word for it. The surgeon's register colours the noticing (a cost asked as a direction answered with the pot and the weather, a carried arm as a record in muscle that knows weight and not cost, the private file turned out as instruments on a towel, likenesses taken down one at a time before they can stand up and call themselves a rule, a hand going up toward a note and held there for one counted breath) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line — the old life stays offstage — and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector or back-room interior, no new hearing, no tenth stopping, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause, no calling of the loan, no payer named, no private record read and no ending

scenes.title: The Figure Gone Up the Road
scenes.synopsis: First entry, first dated heading and drop capital: Day 192, Ember 13, Thirdday, before first grey through the morning under the Vail kiln-house roof and out into the Clay Yard. Do not recap the close of Chapter 46. Open on the hand outside the wool going up an inch toward the note of water over water and coming down against the fold, the count at one hundred and ninety-one exact, complete and unspent carried into the new day; the boy is one hundred and ninety-two days old and six months and twelve days and nobody under any roof says so (T071/T072). First smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool with the sour mineral breath of the unswept corner; first sound the kiln drawing breath in fours with a gap, not a bell (T061/T082). The crust lies leathery two inches from his ear with its empty place unnamed and no third, the thread of drool frozen and unwiped, cold stopped at cheek, temple and the small bare joint at the wrist where the wool rides back, the afterdrop waiting on a warming nobody in this house will perform. The carried fire under the floor answers four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and ninety-two days (T088); through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings; overhead the boards keep four nails, four and a knot the width of a thumb — three counts in three places that do not become one. Sella Vail gives every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, says the house where another woman would say I, keeps her half-pace, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze without touching it, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with her hand resting a half-beat longer at the setting, tells the carried fire it is the thaw and says The house will keep it (T058/T079). The widow's mark hangs where it hung, touched once before the kiln on Ember 1 and at no shelf, well, rack, road, basket, yard, afternoon or dusk since, because a morning in the quiet days after the reading is not an opening. A neighbour asking what the firing will want now the account has gone up is sent to the pot and the weather with Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there. The house has said it, and carries the question away level, nothing priced, refused or entered (T077). The yard goes around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the space beneath the lowest rack with its broken birth-slates, the pan's gone round ring, the bare dark trough whose water is called weather and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, each with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092/T098 carried). The printed one in twelve stands unchallenged and the true subtraction sits in Berr's locked box up the road; Hessa's slate lies delivered unread at Greybank and the clerk stays set at the landing, all held and not revisited on stage (T015/T041/T047, T080, T090 held). Nothing is joined, paid, named, opened, called, spent or ended.

scenes.title: Six Hearings and a Fifth Place
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 192, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the kindling, the hearth, the bed and the clay road at the going of the light. The afternoon thins without ending, losing its edges the way water goes off a stone that has held the sun, heat staying longest in the low places. Sella stands with her back to the basket and moves her lips along a row with two unnamed gaps, the old space at the row's end and the palm's breadth that came in on the night of Seed 6, gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar without touching it, and keeps her finger from beneath the front edge so the charcoal tally stays unread, uncounted, uncopied (T100); the Day 166 held beat stays where it was left, an afternoon and a woman's back turned not the same as that night. She tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, stands a moment counting under her breath toward no opening — the small intake, the hold, the letting go — sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and does not look toward the bed (T058/T079). At the kindling the small knife lies at the edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it; Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, says Yes, house to an early thaw and a late while wanting the late because it puts off the paying, and sweeps the collector's road without turning; no collector comes. His chest is tight since the dark; the breath from Seed 16 stands unspent at the top of every reach with the small interval where a breath should have gone in and had not; the ear-sentence comes to the threshold of the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, drawn and not spent; the nine stoppings stay nine objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned and the loan is still uncalled (T036/T076). His stroke goes over the flagstones and the shallow bright patch without the half-check and the stones keep the place where it stopped. In the wheel-shed Jorra gives the men unnamed before first grey no name, comes through with grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent finger, keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray, tells the wheel it does not care whose hands, tells a pot You'll do, knows its note three turns ahead and withholds it from a man on the wrong wind; when Sella's sentence goes low and unfinished his bent finger stands in the cold damper until the end reaches the pot — a remembered holding, not a new change, not paired with Day 161 or Day 166 or Day 171 (T035/T031/T062). The two shut-room tellings stay two with no third (T065/T095). The sweet edge of lead glaze comes up off High Kiln on a wrong wind and is answered as a direction and goes out on the same wind; the pot that sang itself out early stands swept around and is not made an omen or a lesson (T064 held, T061/T082). The stone lies back in its unmarked pot in the Debt Loft, cold and unreconciled by not trying, which is not forgiving, and from below the boy keeps only the remembering of the small dry scrape on a place of its own, not a holding made again (T006). At the going of the light Sella carries him home up the clay road, woodsmoke before and river wind behind, going wide around the pan's gone place, the bare trough, the rack space, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed with a look and a wide step and no number; under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face, leaves the thread frozen, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting, tells the fire it is the thaw, banks the coals and does not touch the mark; the two rooms do not touch. In the small hours he turns out the file as a man lays instruments on a towel: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth from a person and no seventh; three near-full answers advanced and unpaid; nine stoppings as objects with no tenth; three held changes on three places, the loft-sill scrape on a fourth and the carried man's pale line on a fifth, exact, complete and worth nothing, not joined to the sweet wind, the dust, the pot that sang early, the sixth green, the foundling's sliver, the pan's ring or any absence. He wants the crust, the breast, the pot handle and a number nobody will speak, and gets none (T060/T086/T097/T100/T006/T064).

scenes.title: The Wrong Wind Answered
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated heading: Day 193, Ember 14, Fourthday, before first grey through the morning at the Vail kiln-house, the drying racks, the yard well, the wheel-shed edge and the Clay Yard. The kiln month's second working week runs on without a boundary drawn; the district keeps calling Tallow the firing month and Ember the kiln month and neither is corrected. The boy is one hundred and ninety-three days old and six months and thirteen days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth is still missing under the floor with its payer unnamed for a hundred and ninety-three days (T088); river, fire and boards keep three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). Hot clay under tallow, wet wool under that, sour Ash breath. Sella feeds him barley gruel from the house's own dish with two fingers behind his ear, wipes the spoon on her sleeve and does not wipe his mouth, gives the instruction to the fire, the pot, the broom and the wool and never to the basket, says the house, keeps her half-pace and her jar-glance without a touch, and sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand (T058/T079). A woman come up from the racks with slip dried pale in the creases of her wrists asks what the pots will want before the kiln month is out and is told to ask the pot and the weather; the question goes away level, nothing entered (T077). The sweet edge rides a wrong wind off High Kiln again and is taken as a direction, not a name and not a cause; nobody says what ailed the man carried out on Day 188, no collector is called, no figure given and no slate opened, and his pale line lies where it was laid (T064 held). Before first grey three or four men unnamed go low into the finger's-width-open back room and get no name; the broken birth-slates lie under the lowest rack entered by nobody and the yard goes around them (T035/T031/T065/T095, T009/T013/T092). Jorra comes through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent finger and under the nails, white in the creases where a fist opened, not bone-coloured slip; he keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray and asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, speaks to the wheel before anyone, tells a pot You'll do, knows its full note three turns ahead and withholds it from a man on a wrong wind who says a pot singing before its time generally sings itself out early; the knowing goes to the near-full tray, advanced and not paid, and no pot is lost. *He's not Vail* stays sealed and the promise of the boy's name to the men who burn slates stays ungiven (T035/T031). Tarn at the kindling keeps the knife at the edge of its sill with six where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, Garl's sentence beside it, Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line and the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holding what light there is and giving it back; he says Yes, house to the early and the late, wants the late, and sweeps without turning (T036/T076). The charcoal waits unread under the shelf and Sella's finger does not go beneath its front edge (T100). The warm stone stays cold in its pot in the loft (T006).

scenes.title: A Fraction at the Reach
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 193, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the kindling, the hearth and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending; heat goes first out of the high air and stays longest under the shelf, behind the pot, in the fold of wool where the boy lies. Sella stands at the shelf with her back to the basket, moves her lips along the row with two gaps and gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing without touching it, keeps her finger from beneath the front edge, tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and does not look toward the bed (T058/T079, T100). At the kindling Tarn brings the ear-sentence all the way to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, draws the breath he should have spent and does not spend it, says Yes, house to the fire and goes on with the broom; the nine stay nine with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the loan uncalled and the seventh year nearer its end than it has ever stood and not given; his stroke goes over the flagstones past the bright patch without the half-check (T036/T076). Jorra's bent finger stands in the cold iron while Sella's unfinished sentence reaches the pot, then moves the tongue a hair's breadth and is left standing — a remembered repetition, not a change made again, not stood up with the other two (T062). The damper is read once more as one piece of iron with two bites, the holding and the taking, with no word in Grathic that would carry both mercies in one mouthful, an object joined to no kiln and entered in no slate (T062/T035). The boy lies at the low angle where the underside of the shelf makes a roof that stops at the edge of his reach. **The chapter's first small movement:** his hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the note of water over water and hesitates there for the length of the small pause in the kiln's breath before it comes down against the fold — a fraction held on a place of its own, not a hearing, not a seventh, not a stopping, not one of the three held changes, not a payment, with no payer named and no cause allowed to stand up out of it (T071/T072, T061/T082). He cannot close the two inches to the pot handle and cannot lift his chin to the crust; the body is allowed to humiliate him even as it moves. At the going of the light Sella carries him home, goes wide around the yard's places with a look and a wide step and no number, sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face and leaves the thread frozen; she does not touch the mark, because a dusk is not an opening. In the small hours the file comes back exact, complete and worthless: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers unpaid, nine stoppings with no tenth, three held changes on three places with the loft scrape on a fourth and the pale line on a fifth, the told bell beside the heard and the told figure beside the paid, the crust's gap, the two shelf gaps, the pan's ring and the field's empty place on trays that do not touch, no third gap and no fourth likeness made a cause (T060/T086/T097/T100/T006/T064).

scenes.title: The Third Quiet Morning
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated heading: Day 194, Ember 15, Fifthday, before first grey through the morning under the Vail roof, at the yard well, the drying racks, the wheel-shed edge and along the clay road. The kiln month's second working week draws toward its end with no boundary drawn. The boy is one hundred and ninety-four days old and six months and fourteen days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire's payer is unnamed for a hundred and ninety-four days (T088); the other two counts stay in their places and do not become one (T061/T082). First smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool, with the sour mineral breath of the unswept corner; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap. Sella's instruction goes to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket; she says the house, keeps her half-pace, glances once at the clay jar without touching it, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting, feeds him from the house's own dish and does not wipe his mouth (T058/T079). The widow's mark hangs where it hung, for a morning and a shelf are not openings and there has been no opening since before the kiln on Ember 1. A woman with a wet pot asks what a wet thing costs set down in the dry heat and is sent to the pot and the weather; another asks what the kiln will want now the figure has gone up the road and is told the house has said it; both go away level with nothing slopped, priced, refused or entered (T077). The yard goes around the clean dark line, the new finer grey called the thaw, the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lie, the pan's gone round ring with no scrape, crumb or chip, the bare dark trough whose water is called weather, the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, and the place the carriers crossed with the glaze-room hand between them, each with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092/T098 carried). A sweetish edge comes off High Kiln on a wrong wind and is answered as a direction; nobody revives the carried man as a cause, calls a collector or names his sickness in Grathic, and the man went out of the yard breathing and went on up the clay road (T064 held). Three or four men unnamed go low into the back room before first grey and get no name; the two shut-room tellings stay two with no third (T035/T031/T065/T095). Jorra's dusty forearms and clean ones stay on one tray, the full note known three turns ahead and withheld from a man on the wrong wind, the knowing advanced and not paid, *he's not Vail* sealed and the promise to the slate-burners ungiven (T035/T031). Tarn's knife stays at the edge of its sill with six where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the ear-sentence short of the word, the nine still nine (T036/T076). The charcoal waits unread under the shelf (T100); the stone lies cold and unreconciled in its loft pot (T006); the crust stays leathery two inches from his ear with its empty place unnamed and no third (T060/T086).

scenes.title: One Breath Held at the Reach
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 194, Ember 15, Fifthday, afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the kindling, the hearth, the bed and the clay road at the going of the light. The afternoon thins without ending. Sella stands with her back to the basket, moves her lips along the row with two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar without touching it, keeps her finger from beneath the front edge so the charcoal stays unread, tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, stands with the back of the pot in her hand counting under her breath toward no opening — the small intake at the top, the hold, the letting go — pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, sets the pot rim out on the board with its handle standing two inches beyond the reaching hand and does not look toward the bed (T058/T079, T100). At the kindling the knife lies at the edge of its sill with six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it; Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, brings the ear-sentence to the threshold of the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, draws the breath and does not spend it, says Yes, house to the fire and goes on; the nine stoppings stand as objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the loan uncalled, his stroke over the flagstones and the shallow bright patch without the half-check (T036/T076). In the wheel-shed Jorra gives the men no name, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, tells the wheel it does not care whose hands, tells a pot You'll do, withholds its note from the wrong wind, and holds his bent finger in the cold damper until Sella's unfinished sentence reaches the pot as a remembered repetition, not a new change (T035/T031/T062). The stone lies back in its unmarked pot in the loft, two years gone and cold, unreconciled by not trying, which is not forgiving; from below the boy keeps only the remembering of the dry scrape on a place of its own, not joined to the three held changes and not made a cause (T006). At the going of the light she carries him home up the clay road, woodsmoke going before her in long low bars and the river wind coming up behind with the taste of water over water, the two passing on the stair of the evening without taking each other's colour or spending a word on either; the instruction goes to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, and the arm that has carried him a hundred and ninety-four mornings keeps the height of the handle, the give of the shoulder and the turn of the wrist at a step's end, a record in muscle that remembers weight and not cost. She goes wide around the pan's gone place, the bare dark trough, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed, each with a look and a wide step and no number; under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, base first and the weight settled the way a woman sets a vessel that must not rock, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without once looking at his face, leaves the thread of drool frozen and unwiped, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting than the setting needed, tells the fire it is the thaw, banks the coals with the back of a broken pot and does not touch the mark, because a dusk is not an opening. The two rooms do not touch. **The chapter's one meaningful change** is lived in the small hours: he turns out the file as a man lays instruments on a towel and finds it exact, complete and worthless — six hearings beside and never among with the sixth from a person and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, nine stoppings as objects with no tenth, three held changes on three places with the loft scrape on a fourth and the carried man's pale line on a fifth, the told bell beside the heard and the told figure beside the paid, the crust's gap, the shelf's two gaps, the pan's ring and the field's empty place on trays that do not touch, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause and no finger of his drawing the line. Then his hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the note of water over water through the finger's-width door and **does not come down at once**: it stays there for the length of one of the breaths Sella counts at her fire in the room that does not touch this one, a small intake at the top, a hold, a letting go, and only then comes down against the fold. It is a change held and unspoken, filed on a place of its own beside the others and never laid across them — not a hearing, not a seventh, not a stopping, not a payment, not one of the three held changes, with no payer named and no doctrine allowed to stand up out of it. He still cannot close the two inches to the pot handle, lift his chin to the crust or speak a number; the body humiliates him and moves by an inch at the same time. One hundred and ninety-four stands exact, complete and unspent in the dark of the wool, spoken by nobody under any roof; cold has stopped at cheek, temple and the small bare joint at the wrist where the wool rides back, and the afterdrop waits on the far side of a warming nobody in this house will perform. The nine stoppings are still nine with no tenth, the Seed 16 breath is still held, the charcoal still waits under the shelf for a hand that is not hers and a day that has not come, the mark was touched once before the kiln and at no other hour, and the cost of the man carried out stands entered nowhere. Nothing has been joined, named, opened, called, spent or ended.
